$comment: `accepted` is the flat list the analyzer reads: a shipped Rust vulnerability listed
here does not fail --strict. `entries` carries the REASON for each, which is the part
a reviewer needs and the derivation cannot supply.
This list may only SHRINK. Fixing an advisory removes its entry (the gate reports a
still-listed-but-resolved entry as STALE). A NEW shipped vulnerability must be patched,
not appended — appending is how a gate becomes a parking lot. Re-seed only from
`node scripts/check-rust-advisories.mjs --list`, never from a hand grep.
WHY THESE THREE ARE SEEDED RATHER THAN PATCHED: they are pre-existing debt that
accrued while NOTHING scanned the Rust graph at all — the very gap this gate closes.
Seeding a measured-green baseline first is the same precedent the npm sibling set, and
it is what lets the guard be wired without red-pinning the fleet on debt it slept
through. Each reason below names the concrete next action, not a shrug.
Only advisories WITHOUT `database_specific.informational` appear here. The 17
unmaintained + 1 unsound notices over the same 615 crates are reported by the gate and
never gate, so they are deliberately absent from this file.
seededFrom: node scripts/check-rust-advisories.mjs --list against papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock (615 crates, OSV.dev crates.io ecosystem) — 21 advisory clusters, 3 gating vulnerabilities, 18 informational

RUSTSEC-2024-0429.reason: Unsoundness in glib::VariantStrIter's Iterator/DoubleEndedIterator impls. Fixed in glib 0.20.0, but papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml pins `glib = "0.18"` DELIBERATELY, with the stated reason that it must stay on the same 0.18 line tauri/wry already use so there is exactly one GTK in the process (D-009, the embedded native terminal view). Bumping to 0.20 splits the GTK/glib ABI in-process — precisely the forced feature-removing upgrade WI-2144851 excludes. Deferred until tauri/wry themselves move to the glib 0.20 line, at which point the pin is bumped WITH them, not ahead of them. NOTE: this cluster is OSV alias pair GHSA-wrw7-89jp-8q8g (classified a vulnerability, GHSA severity MODERATE) + RUSTSEC-2024-0429 (classified informational 'unsound'); the gate resolves the disagreement fail-closed to vulnerability, which is why it appears here at all.

RUSTSEC-2026-0194.reason: Quadratic run time when checking a start tag for duplicate attribute names (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H = 7.5). TWO instances, neither a direct dependency. (1) quick-xml 0.39.4 via plist 1.9.0 <- tauri: PATCHABLE NOW and semver-compatible — `cargo update -p plist` was DRY-RUN VERIFIED 2026-09-05 to resolve plist 1.9.0 -> 1.10.0 and quick-xml 0.39.4 -> 0.41.0, exactly the fixed version, touching 2 packages. Not applied in this change because papercusp-desktop is a submodule whose src-tauri target/ is COLD (0 rlibs), so a lockfile edit to a SHIPPED artifact could not be build-verified here without a full ~615-crate Tauri build on a box running 74 agents; an unverified lockfile bump to the shipped desktop is the worse risk. (2) quick-xml 0.37.5 via tauri-winrt-notification 0.7.2 <- notify-rust <- tauri-plugin-notification, which requires ^0.37 and therefore CANNOT take 0.41 without a tauri-winrt-notification bump (0.8.1 exists upstream) — so patching plist alone does not clear this row, which is why both instances are recorded together. Next action: apply the plist bump behind a real `cargo check`, then re-run this gate; the entry becomes STALE only when BOTH instances are off the vulnerable range.

RUSTSEC-2026-0195.reason: Unbounded namespace-declaration allocation in NsReader enables memory-exhaustion denial of service (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H = 7.5). Same two quick-xml instances and the same fixed version (0.41.0) as RUSTSEC-2026-0194, and it clears with that one or not at all. Stated independently rather than by reference, because an entry that delegates its justification reads as justified without being so: (1) quick-xml 0.39.4 via plist 1.9.0 <- tauri is patchable by `cargo update -p plist` (dry-run verified 2026-09-05: plist 1.10.0 pulls quick-xml 0.41.0); NOT applied here because papercusp-desktop is a submodule whose src-tauri target/ is COLD, so this lockfile edit to a SHIPPED artifact could not be build-verified without a full ~615-crate Tauri build, and an unverified bump to the shipped desktop is the worse risk. (2) quick-xml 0.37.5 via tauri-winrt-notification 0.7.2 requires ^0.37 and cannot take 0.41 without a tauri-winrt-notification bump. Next action: apply the plist bump behind a real `cargo check`, then re-run this gate.
